sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Hungarian verbs change according to the subject. In the indefinite present, common first-person forms often end in -ok/-ek/-ök.

Notice Dolgozom ends in -om, not -ok, even though Tanulok — also ‘I’ + verb — does take -ok. That’s not a typo: dolgozik belongs to a special class of ‘ik-verbs’ that swap the regular -ok/-ek/-ök for -om/-em/-öm in the first person. You’ll run into more of these (eszik → eszem, ‘I eat’), so it’s worth clocking the pattern now.
